//: The package at its own floor. Run it as the FIRST of three passes:
pyright -p pyrightconfig.json
pyright -p pyrightconfig-hook39.json
pyright -p pyrightconfig-shape38.json
Where a new file goes. This config includes whole DIRECTORIES, so
anything added under src/, tests/ or tools/ is covered here with no
edit. The other two are the opposite — explicit file lists — and each
names the files one lower interpreter may EXECUTE.
pyrightconfig-hook39.json must name every file a 3.9 interpreter may
execute. That is two entry points: the recall hook, and `memkit.cli`,
because the plugin's `bin/memkit` runs the dispatcher on the interpreter
the hook wrapper resolved. So `src/memkit/cli.py` belongs in that list
and is in it. Add a module either entry point imports, add it there too,
or its 3.9 floor is unchecked and the failure lands on a stock macOS as a
hook that silently retrieves nothing. A module that merely imports one of
them does not belong there — cli.py importing the hook does not put the
hook's importers on the hook's path.
pyrightconfig-shape38.json is one file and stays one file: only
`tools/harness_shape.py` is piped into a 3.8 interpreter on somebody
else's host. A second file belongs there only if a 3.8 interpreter
EXECUTES it, and nothing else here answers below 3.9.
Add anything else and there is nothing to do.
